title: U.S. House, District 25
what_it_does: Represents Florida's 25th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives; votes on federal laws and spending.
verified_ballot_note: Newly drawn district. Roster from CBS Miami, Boca Daily News and Boca Raton Tribune: Scott Singer (R) vs. Jared Moskowitz (D). County makeup inferred from coverage (Boca Raton-based; Rep. Wasserman Schultz's Weston home no longer inside it) and not independently confirmed. No NPA candidate identified; absence unconfirmed. Sources: https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/2026-florida-primary-district-25-republican-scott-singer/ ; https://bocadailynews.com/2026/08/former-boca-raton-mayor-singer-wins-gop-congressional-primary ; https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/live-updates/2026-florida-primary-live-updates-results/ Florida adopted a new congressional map (passed Apr 29, 2026, signed May 4, 2026) that reworked 21 of 28 districts; county descriptions here reflect post-redistricting reporting where found (https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-05-06/breakdown-changes-for-florida-new-congressional-map).

candidates.name: Scott Singer
candidates.background: Scott Singer served as mayor of Boca Raton from 2018 until his congressional run; his campaign says the city cut its property tax rate seven straight years under him. He launched a bid against U.S. Rep. Jared Moskowitz in the old CD 23 in December 2025 and pivoted to the new 25th District after the 2026 map passed. He won the five-way Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary with 11,758 votes (about 31%), narrowly ahead of George Moraitis (10,299) and Dan Franzese (9,634), with Joe Kaufman (4,630) and Raven Harrison (1,183) trailing.
candidates.primary_result: Won Aug 18, 2026 Republican primary with 11,758 votes (~31%) over Moraitis (10,299), Franzese (9,634), Kaufman (4,630) and Harrison (1,183) (Boca Daily News; CBS Miami)

candidates.name: Jared Moskowitz
candidates.photo_source: congress.gov member portrait (bioguide ID from memory, unverified)
candidates.background: Jared Moskowitz has served in Congress since 2023 representing the 23rd District and previously was Florida's emergency management director and a state representative, where he worked on the 2018 school-safety law passed after the Parkland shooting. After the 2026 redistricting he ran in the new 25th and won the Aug. 18, 2026 Democratic primary over Oliver Larkin, a challenger backed by Democratic Socialists. He joined and later co-chaired the House DOGE caucus, which he declared 'dead' in May 2025. Note: he is a sitting member of Congress but the new CD 25 is an open seat.
candidates.primary_result: Won Aug 18, 2026 Democratic primary over Oliver Larkin (CBS Miami); percentage not captured
